newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down across the board on Friday on weak market sentiment, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 23,460 yuan ($2,828) per tonne, losing 140 yuan.
It opened at 23,500 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 23,530 and a low of 23,400.
July fell 140 to 22,800, August 120 to 23,060, September 80 to 23,320, November 60 to 23,560 and December 50 to 23,550.
Combined volume rose to 51,730 tonnes from 45,940.
Copper opened higher but fell steadily for most of the session, with most investors selling short, being pessimistic about the short term market trend, traders said.
"More and more investors believe copper will fall gradually due to the coming summer season," one trader said. "Technical charts also indicate a downward trend."
The demand for copper usually decreases in June and July.
Physical prices are around 22,800 yuan per tonne in Shanghai the area, down from 23,000 yuan last week, traders said.
Traders noted domestic copper prices were continuing weak despite recent rises on the London Metal Exchange.
"Weak demand and hedging selling are responsible for the recent weak market trend in Shanghai," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper to fall further in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down across the board.
June fell 50 to 14,500, July fell 10 to 14,690, August 150 to 14,800, September 100 to 14,950, October 100 to 14,950, and November 350 to 14,950.
Combined volume rose to 2,930 tonnes from 1,780.
